summary.one_liner: A Claude Code plugin that turns a URL plus CSS selectors into annotated screenshots, flow GIFs/MP4s, terminal recordings and before/after composites, pixel-verifying each output before saving.
summary.what_it_does: Takes a page URL and CSS selectors, measures the DOM, and draws annotations (rectangles, callouts, arrows, badges, blur, zoom) placed deterministically on the target element. Its "auto" mode discovers salient elements on a page (heading, primary action, nav, metrics, hero, cards) without selectors and annotates each one. The "rec" tool renders narrated flow GIFs or MP4s from JSON steps covering clicks, fills, scrolling, camera moves, spotlight, and state effects such as countup, sparkline and confetti. "tape" records terminal sessions via vhs, "compose" builds before/after comparisons, and "shrink" and "beautify" optimize file size and add browser-window or social-card frames. Each artifact is validated by a pixel check (PASS/FAIL) and a failed capture is treated as an error rather than saved.
use_cases: annotated screenshots for documenting a UI change
narrated GIF or MP4 walkthrough of a web flow
visual proof that a page element renders correctly
before/after comparison images for a pull request
terminal session recording as a GIF
social card or browser-frame wrapping of screenshots
notable: Bundles its own headless Chromium, so no browser MCP or credentials are needed
Deterministic annotation placement computed from DOM measurements, with no pixel guessing or retry loop
Every output is pixel-verified (vcheck) and exits non-zero on FAIL
Flow recordings support a viewport camera, spotlight, live-updating glossary panels and offline virtual-clock rendering
--batch mode renders many captures in one browser launch
caveats: Requires a one-time Playwright and Chromium download of about 90MB from npm and Microsoft's CDN on first run
Offline rendering is best for static or text-heavy takes; motion effects like confetti and sparkline need a realtime take
Terminal recordings additionally require the optional vhs tool
keywords: make a gif of my app
